**Solution 1 (√5) is wrong.** Let g(θ) = Re[R₁e^{iθ} + R₂e^{2iθ} + R₃e^{3iθ}], where R_m are the autocorrelations of the coefficients, so |f|² = 4 + 2g. Since |f|² has mean 4, g has mean 0. Its e^{3iθ} coefficient has modulus 1/2, so g contains cos 3θ up to a normalization. Using the nonnegative weight w = (1 + cos 3θ)/2π, which integrates to 1, gives ∫g·w = 1/2. So max g ≥ 1/2, i.e. M² ≥ 5. Equality would force g = 1/2 almost everywhere, contradicting mean 0. Hence M > √5, and √5 is not attainable.

**Solutions 2 and 3 (M² = 4 + 16√3/9 ≈ 7.08) are wrong.** Their minimum is beaten by an explicit polynomial. Take f(z) = z³ + bz² + cz + 1 with b ≈ −0.7135 + 0.7006i and c ≈ 0.9635 + 0.2676i (all unimodular, with b + c̄ = 0.25 + 0.433i). Evaluating directly:
- f(1) = 2.25 + 0.968i, so |f(1)|² ≈ 6.00.
- At θ ≈ −0.13, |f|² ≈ 6.17.
- Sampling the whole circle, the maximum of |f|² is about 6.17, so max|f| ≈ 2.48.

Since 2.48 < 2.66 ≈ √(4 + 16√3/9), the value claimed by Solutions 2 and 3 is not the minimum.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
